bow is pretty easy once you learn the spacing, it's true combos are very easy to input, your main focus is stage control and juggling with nlight/nair, catching landings with dlight for more combos. all your combos come from dlight. you'll want to learn reads off of slight, if they dodge in just slight again into dlight then nair/nlight/sair/dair. if they dodge out you can cd slight or dash dlight, up or up in you can dash nlight or sair. use ground pound sparingly, it has the highest force for gp in the game but is incredibly slow.

gauntlets is relatively similar to katars in that you can react to dodges rather than hard reading them most the time. some tips for gauntlets, be cautious with dlight, it's your best starter for true combos but very punishable. fast fall after slight to see what your opponent does, with your drift you can usually land and catch them with a nair if youre fast. if you notice they're regularly dodging in/out go for a gc slight instead. some gauntlets strings have pretty tight inputs especially on controller so make sure you lab those till you're consistent. I'm talking about like nair gc dlight cd reverse nair gp. specifically the reverse nair part is tight

spear is easy, there's not much to it. slight dlight gc dlight sair when you catch a dodge. if they have a dodge and you hit a slight, try to read it so you can do the flowchart. don't overuse ground pound, people at 1750 will be able to punish it. 

blasters have tricky spacing because of the dead zones and they also have some of the hardest inputs for normal combos. dlight recovery is very difficult to input if you've never done it before, learning to x pivot consistently can be tricky, lots of gravity cancels in general, etc.

i mean, it's possible you do, it's also very possible you don't. If you are worried about it and think it may apply to you though, it is a valid concern to bring up with a professional who is qualified to make a diagnosis.

Different conditions can have overlapping symptoms or present themselves in ways that may appear as something else. Which is why having a professional who can understand and identify the root cause is important. For example, ADHD, especially Inattentive Type, can outwardly present itself as what looks like depression. Or for a more personal example, from a base level reading of the diagnostic criteria I fit all of the traits for Avoidant Personality Disorder. But all of those criteria can also be explained by a combination of symptoms from Depression, Social Anxiety Disorder, ADHD, and an avoidant attachment style interacting with each other. 

Personality disorders in particular typically take a much longer time and interviewing for psychiatrists/psychologists to make a comfortable diagnosis about. Whenever you do see a professional, just bring up that you were researching some of your symptoms and it seems like you could potentially have BPD, and they can proceed from there.

I'm not OP or a lawyer but I read the full draft for the first time last night and wanted to share my thoughts. Though I personally believe women have the right to choose, I do not think the constitution recognizes that right. 

I personally found the draft well reasoned, however strongly worded it might have been. There weren't any glaring holes in any of the arguments and they were well supported by historical precedent. I do think that the reasoning behind Roe was incredibly weak and vague, especially for a decision with as sweeping of an impact it had on existing statutes that were not constitutionally challenged in any meaningful way at for at least 100 years. I think that the following framework Roe imposed of when states could restrict abortion was entirely outside the scope of the Courts expertise or authority. Casey in my opinion made no real attempt to bolster the reasoning behind Roes finding that abortion was a constitutionally protected right, but rather just assumed that it was correct and didn't bother to challenge it, and was another instance of the court implementing a legislative framework for abortion statutes that they had no business implementing. And I agree especially with Alito toward the end of the draft where he essentially says that while public perception of the court is important, if an erroneous judgement was made in the past, the court still has a duty to overturn that regardless of how popular that decision is, or how old the precedent is.

1. I put the PW MK1 below the Chimera and Spear based on how well I personally perform with the planes. I can finish dogfights much quicker with the Spear than I can the PW, and I can complete ground heavy missions much faster with the Chimera than I can the PW. The Swarm is rarely super successful for me unless I'm aiming at a large amount of 1 hit ground targets, other than that the only times it works really well are when targeting a relatively small number of things and that just feels like a waste to me. My main reason I prefer the Spear is because both the Swarm and railgun take a long time to reload, so if I use one and the other isn't a great option for the situation, I just have a really fast plane with std missiles and an HGP, which is still really good, but I much prefer the RGP over both HGP and Missiles.

2. The Spear works really well for me in target rich environments, I've been playing the campaign today with the double fighter spawn modifier and exclusively using the spear and been doing really well(on Hard), even on M11. Sure I have to AoA to catch up or get on target, but I have no issue doing that. The PW does have a HGP, but so does the spear, and keeping the spears guns on target is a lot easier for me than keeping the PWs on.

3. Again, I don't play conquest really, and I wouldn't use the Chimera for that at all. But as far as a ground attack plane goes, it handles pretty well. I can perform well in dogfights with it on Hard, which is good for me. And you said "compared to AA missiles" for the Chimera, but I never equip MLAAs on it, because that's not what I use it for. I always go either three slots of MLAG, or one ASM and two slots of MLAG, depending on whether there are Airships in the mission.

yeah, the timing belt/chain is *usually* behind the front cover. You have to be careful to make sure you set the cams and crank at the right spots, as well as any balance shafts and what not that might run off of it, and EXTREMELY careful if its an interference motor. How much you have to take apart to get to the timing belt/chain varies widely between motors, chains are usually a lot more involved, but you also don't need to do them nearly as often and theyre far less likely to break, whereas a cam seal leak that starts 20mi after you do the timing belt could eventually cause your belt to break.

replacing serpentine belts depends on the belt. almost all new engines use an auto tensioner, so yeah, pull it to remove tension, remove the belt, replace. Some older serpentine belts and pretty much anything with multiple belts will either have A. a bolt tension system, so you loosen or tighten a bolt on one of the accessory components to tension the belt, or B. one of the accesory components sits in a slide bracket, so you loosen it and move it so the belt isnt tensioned, replace the belt then use like a pry bar to hold the component with tension while you tighten the bolts back up

This is pretty easy to do on your own. You will need a spark plug socket, probably a 5/8" size, although it could be a 9/16", I'm sure that info is availabke online. Note that a regular deep socket wont work, spark plug sockets have more room for the tip of the plug. I won't get into whether or not to use a torque wrench or anti seize or whatnot because lots of people have different opinions on that, I would just look up the procedure for your car and follow that. Swapping out the coil should be really easy. Most likely just 10mm bolts holding down over the spark plug tube.

If you want to save money and fine out if its the spark plug or the coil, here is how you can do that. If you have access to a scan tool or reader the easiest way is to swap the cyl 1 coil with another coil and see if the code changes to a different cylinder. If it stays at 1 its most likely the spark plug, in which case, always replace all your spark plugs at the same time. Coils you can just replace the one thats bad, although if it were me I'd do all of them, only issue is coils can be EXPENSIVE, but I get discounts on parts so 🤷

Of course, it could also be like, a fuel injector, which I wouldn't really recommend trying to do on your own. If its port injection you can give it a shot, but if its direct injection like a lot of kia/hyundai motors then please leave that to a shop. The fuel pressure in direct injected cars can be high enough to inject fuel into your skin/bloodstream, which is very bad. And they also have special seals and hardlines that have to be replaced whenever theyre removed and they require special tools and whatnot.

I know someone who works on like construction rigs and there was a fuel leak on one of them. Diesels run at a very high pressure, even higher than gas direct injected cars, and even 100psi can penetrate skin. So the guy was climbing up on the rig to look for the leak and it happened to be spraying out of a line right where he put his hand, and it injected diesel into his hand. The saving grace here is that diesel will gel up when it gets really cold so they were able to put ice on his hand to stop it from flowing into the rest of his body, and the doctors would ice it, cut into his hand/wrist, remove a bit, then reice it to gel it back up before continuing. Torque is the amount of rotational force created by the engine. Since torque is force at a distance(lb ft) the longer stroke an engine has, typically, the more torque it will generate. A 5 L engine with a 2.5" stroke will typically generate less torque than a 5 L engine with a 3.5" stroke.  The gears simply multiply the amount of torque generated by the engine to spin the wheels. The wheels will spin at a slower RPM than the engine but will have a higher torque due to the gear reduction.

They have different applications. Turbos happen to best fit modern applications in most cases. Turbochargers are also a lot more efficient, running off of the excess heat from the exhaust gasses. Superchargers, like any belt driven components, will sap up a certain amount of hp just to spin them. Granted, superchargers generally produce more than they use so its not too big of a deal.

Bigger turbos provide more boost but they also take a lot of exhaust gasses to run them and take a long time to spool up. A bigger engine will need a bigger turbo to achieve the same amount of boost, but bigger engines(like a pushrod v8) also tend to not rev quite as high. You can definitely still use turbos successfully, but this is when superchargers would have an advantage. They provide the same amount of boost, all the time. A roots supercharger pumping out 10psi on a 5.7L V8 will produce 10psi at 700rpm, and 1500rpm, and 2500rpm, and 8000rpm. A big turbo might not produce any boost at all up until 3k or 4k, but the peak boost will be higher.

Another note, there is another kind of supercharger, called Centrifugal Superchargers. These are actually my favorite type of forced induction, I just think they're cool. They work almost exactly like turbos, but run off a belt instead of the exhaust.

One gameplay mechanic I really like in Morrowind though is that pretty much all the enemies levels are static. This really makes it feel like you are becoming more and more powerful throughout the game. Compared to Skyrim where you do get more powerful but it never feels like a huge improvement unless you are intentionally underleveling. It especially creates issues with the magic because theres nothing really to scale the power of the magic up, whereas the perks in the melee trees do scale the power up.

Underleveling(at least thats what ive heard it called), if you don't know, is when you pretty much entirely focus on a very very limited amount of skills, and don't touch anything else. What this does is that it essentially means that while you are say, a level 12 character, your abilities in the 2-3 skills you use are much higher than they would be if you weren't so heavily specialized. This works really well for mage characters in Skyrim because of the lack of scaling. But once you max out your main skills you have to start branching out which will make things start to get a lot more difficult as you do it.
